newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK final Q3 GDP, Q2 trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK final Q3 GDP, Q2 trade data.

text.p: Following is a selection of reactions to UK final third-quarter GDP data showing the annual growth rate revised up to 2.4 percent from the previous 2.3 percent estimate and a Q2 current account surplus of 792 million stg vs previous 457 million estimate:

"The main numbers are much as expected with no revisions quarter-on-quarter. Two points of slight concern -- consumer spending rose by 1.1 percent on the quarter. That will cause some nervousness about the contents of next week's budget, and secondly we saw a very sharp rise in the GDP deflator."
"This is indicative of a general upturn in inflation. So although the headline numbers are as expected, I don't think we can take every much comfort from the detail."

"On the whole the numbers are pretty well in line with expectations. The breakdown is relatively positive in that it shows a fairly decent gain of 1.1 percent in consumer spending, suggesting that retail sales in the third quarter gave a slightly misleading negative impression of consumer sentiment. Overall consumption appears to be picking up rather more strongly. If there are any messages, it suggests that the overall shape of the way the economy is evolving probably increases the risk that interest rates will have to go up again in front of the election."
